description: Somos o Uai-Fi: a conexão mais estável entre Uberlândia e o resto do universo. Sinal forte do Cerrado até Marte, sem cair nem quando passa nuvem. Movidos a café, pão de queijo e dados da NASA, transformamos informação complicada em algo que qualquer um entende, sô. Se der erro, a gente reinicia o roteador. Se funcionar de primeira, a gente desconfia. Senha da rede? Só pra quem acredita que a próxima fronteira começa aqui, uai. 🚀📶
summary: Uai-Fi maps Brazilian places that can stand in for the Moon and Mars. Classic analogs are always the same few sites (Atacama, Antarctica, Iceland), while Brazil, with craters, iron-rich soils, caves, dunes and a large semi-arid region, has never been scanned systematically. We built a Moon/Mars reference table (temperature, regolith, relief, sunlight, rain, water, wind, radiation, fire), scored 14 under-studied Brazilian sites on 8 dimensions into a 0-100 similarity to Mars and to the Moon, and matched each site to the part of a base it can train: farming, habitats, geology, astrobiology, mobility or resources. We also scanned Brazil on a 2,729-point grid with NASA AppEEARS (MODIS LST, NDVI, burned area, SRTM). First results (558 points, northern and northeastern Brazil) point to the semi-arid Northeast as the strongest new analog region, next to two of our researched sites. For every site we state where the analogy breaks.
details: WHAT IT DOES: Finds and characterizes Brazilian terrestrial analogs for Moon and Mars bases. Instead of asking whether a site matches the Moon or Mars in everything (none does), we ask which dimensions it matches and which mission it can train. HOW IT WORKS: (1) Reference table of 16 Moon/Mars conditions with Earth values and sources (NASA fact sheets, LRO Diviner, Phoenix lander chemistry, TES hematite). (2) 14 under-studied Brazilian sites (Araguainha and Serra da Cangalha impact craters, Carajas iron caves, Iron Quadrangle hematite, Peruacu and Toca da Boa Vista caves, Cabaceiras semi-arid, Lencois Maranhenses and Sao Francisco dunes, Nhecolandia soda lakes, Lagoa Salgada stromatolites, Pocos de Caldas caldera, Uberlandia basalt soils, Embrapa Cerrados) scored 0-3 on soil, relief, aridity, subsurface, water chemistry, life, wind and temperature, weighted into 0-100 Mars and Moon scores plus mission profiles. Top results: Peruacu Caves (Moon 53), Toca da Boa Vista (Moon 49), Carajas (Mars 42), Araguainha crater (Moon 42), Iron Quadrangle (Mars 38). (3) A nationwide 2,729-point grid (0.5 deg) sent to NASA AppEEARS; from MODIS NDVI, day/night land surface temperature and burned area we built a satellite analog index (bare ground + large day-night swing + no fire). The 558 points returned so far rank the semi-arid Northeast highest (day surface 36-38 C, NDVI 0.31-0.41 vs 0.73 median), next to Cabaceiras and Toca da Boa Vista, confirming the research ranking. (4) A Plan B pipeline with NASA POWER climatology and SRTM relief. IMPACT: Gives mission planners new, accessible, low-cost analogs in Brazil and an honest list of where each analogy breaks (no vacuum, extreme cold, low gravity or ice). TOOLS: Python (pandas, matplotlib), NASA AppEEARS API, NASA POWER API, OpenTopoData SRTM, Leaflet map. FUTURE: finish the national scan, add SGB geology maps, validate top sites in the field.
dataRefs: NASA AppEEARS (MODIS MOD11A2 LST, MOD13Q1 NDVI, MCD64A1 Burned Area, SRTM)
NASA POWER climatology (temperature, precipitation, solar, humidity, wind)
